_meta.note: Add two agent-framework backends — LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK — in BOTH runtimes (py in-process backends/ + plugin subprocess executors/), following the agno/crewai pattern: two-method contract (execute/refute), graceful degrade when the lib is absent, native file tool with a FILE-block fallback, keyless-testable via Ollama. Backends are not a parity surface, so parity is unaffected (must stay green). Gate cmds are behavioral and non-side-effecting.

tasks.title: LangGraph backend
tasks.description: Add py/src/heartbeat/backends/langgraph.py (in-process) and plugin/templates/executors/langgraph_exec.py (subprocess wire) — execute/refute, graceful degrade, FILE-block writing (reuse _fileblocks), provider ollama|openai via langchain-ollama / a chat model, fd-1→stderr hygiene in the subprocess script.

tasks.title: OpenAI Agents SDK backend
tasks.description: Add py/src/heartbeat/backends/openai_agents.py and plugin/templates/executors/openai_agents_exec.py — same contract; provider ollama (via the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint, keyless) or openai (key).

tasks.title: Register + extras
tasks.description: Register the backends: py backends/__init__.py _KNOWN + name→module mapping (openai-agents→openai_agents); hb-exec.js defaultCmd cases; add langgraph and openai-agents optional-dependencies to py/pyproject.toml.

tasks.title: Python degrade tests
tasks.description: Add py/tests/test_backends_frameworks.py: each backend module imports, and execute/refute degrade to protocol-valid JSON ({ok:false}/{refuted:false}) when the framework lib is absent.

tasks.title: Node validity/degrade tests
tasks.description: Add T47 (LangGraph) and T48 (OpenAI Agents) to tests/run-tests.sh: the executor scripts are valid python and degrade to protocol-valid JSON without the lib; bootstrap ships them under .hb/executors/.

tasks.title: Live proof against Ollama
tasks.description: Install the libs in venvs and run py/real-backend.py for langgraph and openai-agents against a local Ollama model; record the outcome (a model writes code, a behavioral gate runs it).

tasks.title: Docs + version + package
tasks.description: Document the two backends in docs/dev-python.md, the SKILL backends line, and STATUS.md; bump plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json + marketplace.json to 1.14.0 and py/pyproject.toml to 0.6.0; rebuild and extract-test the package.

GATE_FB0.desc: Both backends exist in both runtimes and are registered.

review.prompt: Refute that FB0 is done: do the backends REALLY implement execute AND refute for both runtimes, or a stub? Do they degrade to protocol-valid JSON when the lib is missing (import lazy, not at module top)? Is the subprocess script hygienic (only JSON on stdout)? Are they actually registered so `hb exec --backend langgraph|openai-agents` resolves?

criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from heartbeat.backends import get; assert get('langgraph') and get('openai-agents')"

criteria.desc: both backends import and expose callable execute and refute (py)
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "import importlib; m1=importlib.import_module('heartbeat.backends.langgraph'); m2=importlib.import_module('heartbeat.backends.openai_agents'); assert callable(m1.execute) and callable(m1.refute) and callable(m2.execute) and callable(m2.refute)"

GATE_FB1.desc: Degrade/validity tests pass in both suites.

criteria.desc: node suite covers the new executors (T47/T48 groups PASSED)
criteria.cmd: out=$(bash "$PROJECT_DIR/tests/run-tests.sh" 2>&1); printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q 'GROUPS-PASSED:.* T47 ' && printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q 'GROUPS-PASSED:.* T48 '

GATE_FB2.desc: Documented, versioned, both suites + parity green.
